commands.desc: Show the installed Google ADK version
commands.tooltip: Prints the google-adk package version (e.g. 2.6.3). ADK 2.x is the current generation; the 1.x line (1.38.0) is still maintained in parallel for Vertex AI users. Check this before reading docs, since 2.x renamed several 1.0 commands.

commands.desc: Run an agent once with a single query
commands.tooltip: Executes the agent in the given directory against the query and prints the conversation. AGENT is positional (the agent directory or module) and QUERY is the second positional argument — ADK 2.x removed the old --text flag from ADK 1.0. Runs as the invoking user, so test as the service user for deployed apps.

commands.desc: Run an agent reusing a named session
commands.tooltip: Continues a previous session instead of starting fresh, keeping conversation history and tool state. The session ID must be a valid Python identifier (no hyphens — use underscores). Sessions persist, so the same ID resumes the same conversation across runs.

commands.desc: Run an agent and persist the session
commands.tooltip: Saves the completed session so a later run with --session_id or --resume can pick it up. Use with --session_id to control the name. Useful for reproducing bugs: save the failing turn, then replay it after a code change.

commands.desc: Run an agent with a SQLite session store
commands.tooltip: Points the session service at a SQLite database file instead of the default local storage. ADK 2.x uses SQLAlchemy connection URIs: sqlite:///path for a file, memory:// for in-memory, and agentengine:// to connect to Vertex AI Agent Engine. The same URI flag works on adk api_server.

commands.desc: Run an agent with an in-memory session store
commands.tooltip: Forces a throwaway in-memory session service — every run starts empty and nothing persists. Ideal for automated tests and CI smoke checks where leftover state would pollute results. Sessions vanish when the process exits.

commands.desc: Run an agent from a recorded session file
commands.tooltip: Replays a JSON file of initial events or session input (a SessionInput or conversation transcript) as the starting state. Combined with --save_session this gives a capture-and-replay loop for debugging: record a failing conversation, replay it against a patched agent, and compare.

commands.desc: Resume an agent from a saved session file
commands.tooltip: Continues a previously exported session (the file produced by --save_session) rather than starting a new conversation. The agent picks up its earlier context, variables, and tool results. Distinct from --replay, which injects events as the initial state.

commands.desc: Start the ADK agent API server
commands.tooltip: Launches the FastAPI server that exposes agents over HTTP at the given port (default 8000). Production deployments typically wrap get_fast_api_app() in a custom FastAPI app instead (the Hosty pattern) so auth and a UI can be added; the built-in server is the quick way to expose agents for testing.

commands.desc: Start the ADK API server bound to localhost
commands.tooltip: Binds the server to a specific interface. Binding to 127.0.0.1 keeps agents private to the machine — the standard setup when a reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx) terminates TLS and forwards to the app, exactly how Hosty runs behind Caddy on port 8080.

commands.desc: Start the API server with the A2A endpoint
commands.tooltip: Enables the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol endpoint so other agents can discover and call this one over the standard A2A interface. A2A is Google's cross-vendor agent interoperability protocol — enable it when an orchestration agent needs to invoke this agent as a sub-agent.

commands.desc: Start the API server with auto-reload
commands.tooltip: Watches Python files and restarts the server on every change — the dev-loop equivalent of uvicorn --reload. Never enable in production (restarts drop in-flight requests and reload on every file touch). Use adk web for the full dev experience with the Web UI.

commands.desc: Persist API server sessions in SQLite
commands.tooltip: Stores all HTTP sessions in a SQLite database file so conversations survive server restarts. Without it the default local storage applies. Pair with adk migrate session after upgrading ADK, since the schema can change between versions.

commands.desc: Allow a frontend origin via CORS
commands.tooltip: Adds an origin to the CORS allowlist so a browser frontend on another domain can call the agent API. Pass multiple comma-separated origins. Needed when the UI is served from a different origin than the API server, as with Hosty's Caddy frontend.

commands.desc: Mount the API server under a URL prefix
commands.tooltip: Serves all agent endpoints below the given path (e.g. /adk/apps/...). Useful when a reverse proxy routes multiple services on one domain and each needs its own path. The prefix applies to every route the server registers.

commands.desc: Start the API server with debug logging
commands.tooltip: Sets the logging verbosity; debug level prints every request, agent event, and tool call — invaluable when tracing why an agent behaves unexpectedly. The -v shortcut is equivalent to --log_level debug. Levels: debug, info, warning, error, critical.

commands.desc: Start the ADK Web UI dev server
commands.tooltip: Launches the built-in chat UI for agents — the successor to ADK 1.0's adk dev command. Explicitly a development tool: Google documents that the built-in Web UI must not be exposed in production. For a real deployment wrap get_fast_api_app() in a custom app with your own frontend (the Hosty pattern).

commands.desc: Start the ADK Web UI with a custom logo text
commands.tooltip: Brands the dev UI with your own text (or a logo image via --logo-image-url) instead of the default ADK banner. Cosmetic flags for local demos and internal tools. Nothing here changes agent behavior.

commands.desc: Scaffold a new ADK agent app
commands.tooltip: Creates a folder with a prepopulated agent template — the ADK 2.x replacement for ADK 1.0's adk agent command. The generated layout includes an agent module and the structure get_fast_api_app() expects (agents_dir/<name>/agent.py defining root_agent).

commands.desc: Scaffold an agent preconfigured with a model
commands.tooltip: Generates the agent template with the given model wired into the root agent. For Gemini models over the API key path, set GEMINI_API_KEY (and GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=FALSE unless using Vertex). Hosty instead uses LiteLlm with a DeepSeek model for its API routing.

commands.desc: Scaffold an agent for Vertex AI
commands.tooltip: Preconfigures the template for Vertex AI by baking the Google Cloud project and region into the agent's model config. Add --api_key to stay on the API-key path instead. Vertex mode needs gcloud application-default credentials at runtime.

commands.cmd: adk deploy cloud_run --project my-gcp-project --region us-central1 --service_name hosty
commands.desc: Deploy an agent to Cloud Run
commands.tooltip: Builds the agent and deploys it as a Cloud Run service in the given project and region. --with_ui additionally deploys the ADK Web UI; --port sets the container port. Requires gcloud authenticated and Docker available for the image build.

commands.desc: Deploy an agent plus Web UI to Cloud Run
commands.tooltip: Same as the plain Cloud Run deploy but also ships the ADK Web UI so the deployed agent has a chat interface out of the box. For production, prefer a custom frontend — the built-in UI is dev-oriented. WARNING: deploying overwrites the target service.

commands.cmd: adk deploy agent_engine --project my-gcp-project --region us-central1 --agent_engine_id my-agent
commands.desc: Deploy an agent to Vertex Agent Engine
commands.tooltip: Registers the agent on Vertex AI Agent Engine, Google's managed agent runtime. The positional APP_NAME (the agent folder) comes after the flags. --display_name and --description control how it appears in the Agent Engine console. Requires Vertex AI enabled in the project.

commands.cmd: adk deploy gke --project my-gcp-project --region us-central1 --cluster_name hosty-cluster
commands.desc: Deploy an agent to a GKE cluster
commands.tooltip: Deploys the agent as a workload on an existing Google Kubernetes Engine cluster; --service_name and --app_name set the Kubernetes service and app name. Requires kubectl configured with cluster access. This is the path when you need cluster features Cloud Run cannot offer.

commands.desc: Migrate the session database schema
commands.tooltip: Upgrades a session database to the current ADK schema version. Run it after upgrading google-adk when using a persistent session store (sqlite:// or a database URI) — schema changes between releases can otherwise make old sessions unreadable. Back up the database file first.

commands.desc: Evaluate an agent against an eval set
commands.tooltip: Runs the agent over the given evaluation set (by name or file) and reports pass/fail per case. ADK evals are code-defined assertions over agent turns, carried over from ADK 1.0. Use --print_detailed_results for per-case reasoning and --eval_storage_uri to persist results.

commands.desc: Evaluate an agent with a config file
commands.tooltip: Loads evaluation configuration (models, metrics, parallelism) from a YAML file instead of flags. Lets a team share one eval config across runs and CI. Config overrides defaults; CLI flags still win where both set the same option.

commands.desc: Create an empty evaluation set
commands.tooltip: Creates a named EvalSet that collects related eval cases. Eval sets live in the project's evals storage (default local; --eval_storage_uri overrides). New in ADK 2.x — 1.0 defined evals purely as files, while 2.x adds first-class named sets.

commands.desc: Add eval cases from a scenarios file
commands.tooltip: Appends JSON-serialized scenarios (queries with expected behaviors) to an eval set. --session_input_file adds cases from a recorded SessionInput instead. Lets you grow an eval suite from captured real conversations — replay what broke, then keep it as a regression test.

commands.desc: Run agent test JSON files
commands.tooltip: Executes pytest over the agent test files (agent_test.json / <agent>_test.json) in the current folder, the ADK 2.x replacement for hand-rolled test harnesses. Tests assert on events and tool calls, not just final text. --rebuild regenerates the expected outputs by running the real agent.

commands.desc: Rebuild agent test files from real runs
commands.tooltip: Regenerates the expected results of agent test files by executing the agent for real and recording its behavior. Use carefully: it rewrites what the tests assert, so a buggy agent can bake its own wrong behavior into the expectations. Review the diff before committing.

commands.desc: Optimize the root agent instructions
commands.tooltip: Runs the GEPA (agent instruction optimization) loop over the agent's system instructions using an optimizer LLM and sampler configs, producing an improved instruction set. New in ADK 2.x. Pass --sampler_config_file_path and --optimizer_config_file_path to control the optimization runs.

commands.desc: Run ADK conformance tests
commands.tooltip: Verifies that an agent's behavior matches ADK conformance expectations (the standardized behavior contract used by the ADK test suite). Useful after framework upgrades to catch behavior drift. Requires conformance YAML files generated by adk conformance record.

commands.desc: Record conformance test YAML files
commands.tooltip: Generates ADK conformance test YAML from TestCaseInput definitions, capturing the expected event stream an agent should produce. The companion to adk conformance test — record on a known-good version, then test after changes.

commands.desc: Create an ADK session over HTTP
commands.tooltip: Step one of the two-step ADK HTTP API call: creates a session for the given app, user, and session ID with an empty body. Without this step, POST /run returns 404 'Session not found'. The session ID must be a valid Python identifier (underscores, no hyphens). Sessions persist — reuse the ID for later turns.

commands.cmd: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/run -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $HOSTY_API_KEY" -d '{"app_name":"linux_admin","user_id":"alice","session_id":"dev_session","new_message":{"parts":[{"text":"List running services"}],"role":"user"}}'
commands.desc: Send a user turn to an agent over HTTP
commands.tooltip: Step two of the ADK API pattern: runs the agent with the new user message in an existing session and streams back events. Hosty's API-key auth accepts Authorization: Bearer with the HOSTY_API_KEY value, bypassing TOTP for automation — cron jobs and scripts use this header instead of a session cookie.

commands.cmd: curl -N -X POST http://localhost:8080/run -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $HOSTY_API_KEY" -d '{"app_name":"linux_admin","user_id":"alice","session_id":"dev_session","new_message":{"parts":[{"text":"List running services"}],"role":"user"}}'
commands.desc: Stream an agent run live over SSE
commands.tooltip: The /run endpoint responds with a server-sent events stream; -N disables curl's buffering so each agent event (tool call, partial text, final response) prints as it arrives. Without -N curl waits for the stream to finish. Useful for watching an agent work in a terminal.

commands.desc: Open the ADK API Swagger UI
commands.tooltip: FastAPI serves interactive API documentation at /docs — every endpoint, schema, and example is browsable and executable from the browser. The fastest way to discover the exact JSON shapes the /run and session endpoints expect. The OpenAPI schema itself lives at /openapi.json.

commands.desc: Install the latest google-adk with MCP support
commands.tooltip: Installs ADK 2.x with the mcp extra, which pulls in the MCP (Model Context Protocol) client dependencies needed by McpToolset. Without the extra, MCP tools fail to import. Prefer the pinned form (google-adk[mcp]==2.6.3) for reproducible deployments.

commands.desc: Install a pinned google-adk version
commands.tooltip: Pins the exact ADK version for reproducible deploys — the pattern Hosty uses (google-adk[mcp]==2.6.2). Keep requirements to direct dependencies only: ADK 2.x pulls its own transitive stack, and mixing in the old GCP SDK pins caused dependency-resolution cascades when upgrading from the 2.0.0b1 beta.

commands.desc: Install the latest ADK 1.x release
commands.tooltip: The 1.x line is still published (1.38.0) for existing Vertex deployments and apps not yet migrated. New projects should use 2.x; adk migrate and the migration guide cover the differences. Note the CLI name changes between 1.0 and 2.x — adk dev became adk web, adk agent became adk create.

commands.desc: Serve the custom ADK FastAPI app with uvicorn
commands.tooltip: Runs a custom app built on get_fast_api_app() — the production shape Hosty uses: FastAPI + uvicorn bound to 127.0.0.1 behind Caddy, with auth middleware and a static UI added in main.py. ADK's own adk api_server covers the no-customization case; a custom app is required for real auth and branding.

commands.desc: Serve the ADK app with hot reload
commands.tooltip: Restarts the server whenever a .py file changes — the local dev form of uvicorn. Reload watches the current directory tree, so edit agent.py and the server picks it up without a manual restart. Never use --reload in production.

commands.cmd: su - adkadmin -s /bin/bash -c 'cd /opt/hosty && .venv/bin/adk run linux_admin "List running services"'
commands.desc: Test an ADK agent as the service user
commands.tooltip: Runs adk run as the deployed app's service account so the session database, SSH config, and env are the same ones the service uses. Testing as root instead produces wrong-owner session files ('attempt to write a readonly database') and misses ~/.ssh/config. Always chown the app directory after accidental root runs.

commands.desc: Restart the Hosty ADK agent service
commands.tooltip: Restarts the systemd unit that serves the ADK app. After a restart, subdirectory agents become discoverable only if no stale root-level agent.py exists in the agents directory — ADK switches to single-agent mode when one is present, hiding every subdirectory agent. Remove the stale file, then restart.

commands.desc: Follow the Hosty service logs
commands.tooltip: Streams the adk-agent systemd unit's journal live. Agent stdout, uvicorn access logs, and Python tracebacks all land here — the first place to look when a deployed agent misbehaves. Add -n 200 to see recent history before following.

commands.desc: Deploy the ADK app via rsync
commands.tooltip: Pushes the app tree to the host and removes remote files that no longer exist locally. --delete-excluded additionally purges files excluded by the rsync filter — needed because plain --delete does NOT remove already-synced excluded files (e.g. secrets and caches) on the destination. Verify with a secret-pattern scan after deploying.
